title: How do we get to plug-and-play robots?
gist: Luca Cilio of projectsim argues that generalist robot policies still need heavy manual system engineering (planning, memory, outcome checks) before deployment, citing VoLo, POT-VLA, BATON and Tool-Aligned VLA. Transfer results from Figure Helix 2.5, PI π0.7, Generalist GEN-1.5 and Skild S1, plus AI-driven adaptation (Recursive Harness Distillation, Gemini 4 Argon), point toward plug-and-play robots. He says the missing ingredient is large-scale, physically faithful simulation for training and evaluation, which is what projectsim is building.

themes.theme: Deployment gap between policy and working system

insights.claim: Even when a generalist model is the starting point, deploying a robot still takes a great deal of manual fine-tuning, testing, integration and system engineering, according to a talk by Robot.com CEO Felipe Chavez Cortes at Long Horizon in San Francisco.
insights.speaker: Felipe Chavez Cortes
insights.so_what: Deployment and integration labor, not model capability alone, is the bottleneck for commercial robotics.
insights.quote: even with a generalist model as the starting point, there is still so much manual work around fine-tuning, testing, integration and system engineering before the robot can be deployed
insights.locator: A simple summary of the talk

insights.claim: VoLo pairs π0.5 with a vision-language model that plans and monitors execution, plus grasp and placement tools. In hardware evaluation it completed 18 of 42 trials across 14 tasks, against 6 of 42 for the standalone policy, though more than half of trials still failed.
insights.so_what: Wrapping policies in planners and monitors triples success, but absolute reliability is still far from deployable.
insights.quote: the full system completed 18 of 42 trials across 14 tasks, compared with 6 of 42 for the standalone policy
insights.locator: Some of that manual work goes
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: Checking whether an action is finished is a hard problem in its own right. In a simulated VoLo failure, the monitor concluded that an orange was in a white bowl when it was still on the table, so the system had a progress check but got a wrong answer.
insights.so_what: VLM-based outcome monitors can be confidently wrong, which caps how much autonomy they can safely provide.
insights.quote: The monitor concludes that an orange is in a white bowl while the orange is still on the table.
insights.locator: One of the paper's simulated failures
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: POT-VLA keeps persistent 3D records of task objects and uses them both to guide actions and to check relations such as containment. It tracks uncertainty when objects are occluded and can request another observation, and its policy is fine-tuned to use this information.
insights.so_what: Better outcome checking means co-designing scene memory and the controller, not just bolting on a monitor.
insights.quote: POT-VLA maintains persistent 3D records of task objects, using them both to guide actions and to check relations such as whether one object is inside another.
insights.locator: This is where keeping track
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: A correctly executed skill can still dead-end a task. In BATON's example, a top grasp lifts a can but the combined height blocks placement in a microwave, while a side grasp works. BATON therefore records constraints on skills and their transitions so that the next operation shapes the current choice.
insights.so_what: Long-horizon robot tasks need planning that looks ahead across skill transitions, not just locally successful actions.
insights.quote: The grasp has to serve the placement, which is why BATON records constraints on skills and their transitions
insights.locator: Even a correctly executed action can
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: In several simulated comparisons, putting a planner on top of a conventionally trained policy actually lowered success. Tool-Aligned VLA post-trains policies to execute bounded subtasks, follow precise instructions and report progress, which helps planner and executor work together.
insights.so_what: Hierarchical robot stacks only pay off if the low-level policy is trained for the way it will be called.
insights.quote: In several of its simulated comparisons, putting a planner above a conventionally trained policy actually reduced success.
insights.locator: For that coordination to work
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

themes.theme: Generalization and transfer across homes and robots

insights.claim: In Figure's Helix 2.5 evaluation, tidying, towel folding and bedmaking were fine-tuned on task data collected elsewhere and tested in 30 unseen homes with unseen objects, using one fixed checkpoint per task. With task data, architecture and training held constant, pretraining on Figure's Index human dataset raised full-task completion from 9% to 56%.
insights.so_what: Large human-data pretraining is a major lever on robots working in new environments without per-site retraining.
insights.quote: pretraining on Figure's Index human dataset raised full-task completion from 9% to 56%
insights.locator: The encouraging change is how much
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: PI's π0.7 folds laundry on a dual-arm UR5e setup despite having no laundry demonstrations for that robot. The robot was in training only for other tasks, so the model combined knowledge of the embodiment with knowledge of folding.
insights.so_what: Cross-embodiment transfer cuts the per-robot, per-task data collection cost.
insights.quote: PI's π0.7 folds laundry with a dual-arm UR5e setup despite having no laundry demonstrations for that robot.
insights.locator: Something similar is happening across robot
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: Generalist's GEN-1.5 takes physical demonstrations as prompts. Across ten short tasks, one 3-12 second demonstration gave 59% average success without gradient updates, and five minutes of data per task plus ten fine-tuning steps gave 83%.
insights.so_what: Task-specific adaptation data budgets are falling to seconds or minutes, a key step toward plug-and-play deployment.
insights.quote: one 3–12 second demonstration produced 59% average success without gradient updates. Five minutes of data per task and ten fine-tuning steps produced 83%
insights.locator: When the task itself changes
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: Skild's S1 uses an egocentric video of a person doing a task as the prompt, with selected demonstrations such as plant potting, pancake preparation and kit assembly lasting up to ten minutes, which the company reports were absent from training.
insights.so_what: Human video prompting could let customers specify long jobs without robot teleoperation.
insights.quote: Skild's S1 uses an egocentric video of a person performing the task.
insights.locator: Skild's S1 uses an egocentric
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: Demonstration prompting works because it specifies a job using skills the model already has. A few seconds of task data become useful only because they rest on a much larger body of prior learning, and a demonstration cannot explain why a failure happens.
insights.so_what: The value sits in the pretraining corpus. Diagnosing failures is still unsolved and still needs human engineers.
insights.quote: A demonstration may communicate the intended sequence perfectly without explaining why the can will not fit through the microwave opening.
insights.locator: The remaining difficulty is what happens
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

themes.theme: AI agents taking over adaptation work

insights.claim: In Recursive Harness Distillation, a more capable agent experiments with policy interventions and writes a playbook for a lighter agent, refined from the lighter agent's execution. One revision grew a simple retry instruction into guidance to inspect a failed grasp and check finger-object contact.
insights.so_what: Failure handling that once needed an engineer can be distilled into reusable agent playbooks.
insights.quote: a more capable agent experiments with policy interventions and writes a playbook for a lighter agent
insights.locator: Some of the research is beginning
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: Google's Gemini 4 Argon robotics demos have the model build an articulated MuJoCo twin of a foot-pedal bin, practise balance and pedal stepping, then control a Spot robot to dispose of a can. Another demo has it inspect logs and video of an arm's pick-and-place attempts, test fixes and retry.
insights.so_what: Frontier models are beginning to automate the simulate-diagnose-fix loop of robot deployment.
insights.quote: the model constructs an articulated MuJoCo twin of a foot-pedal bin, practises balance and pedal stepping, then controls a Spot robot to dispose of a can
insights.locator: Google's Gemini 4 Argon robotics demonstrations
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: These are curated demos with substantial instructions and tooling. The last few failures may be exactly the ones a system cannot diagnose, and a confident explanation can be wrong, so the system needs experience and a way to verify that its changes help.
insights.so_what: Treat autonomous robot self-repair demos with caution, because verification is the binding constraint.

themes.theme: Simulation as source of experience and evaluation

insights.claim: Building transferable competence takes far more interactions than any one customer will see. Collecting them physically costs robot time, operators and resets, while simulation can run many parallel copies of a task with varied starting conditions.
insights.so_what: Simulation infrastructure is a structural cost advantage for robotics foundation-model labs.
insights.quote: A lab trying to build that competence needs many more interactions than any one customer will ever see.
insights.locator: That need begins long before deployment.
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: For GR00T N1, NVIDIA reports generating 780,000 simulated trajectories in 11 hours with DexMimicGen, covering 6,500 hours of trajectory time across pre- and post-training datasets, by transforming and replaying segments of human demonstrations and keeping successful attempts.
insights.so_what: Synthetic data can multiply scarce human demonstrations by orders of magnitude.
insights.quote: NVIDIA reports generating 780,000 simulated trajectories in 11 hours using DexMimicGen, covering 6,500 hours of trajectory time
insights.locator: NVIDIA’s work on synthetic training data
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: In SIMPLER, simulated rollouts tracked real-world policy rankings more closely than action-prediction error on recorded demonstrations did, on the tested Google Robot tasks. As policies cover more tasks, testing every version on hardware becomes too expensive.
insights.so_what: Closed-loop simulated evaluation beats offline metrics for choosing robot checkpoints.
insights.quote: In SIMPLER, simulated rollouts tracked real-world policy rankings more closely than action-prediction error on recorded demonstrations did

insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: Training, evaluation and adaptation form one loop over experience. Simulated evaluations identify weak placements or arrangements to target with more data, and GEN-1.5 even used simulated rollouts directly as prompts for a real robot on some tasks without another training run.
insights.so_what: Simulation's value covers the whole lifecycle, from pretraining to post-deployment fixes.
insights.quote: GEN-1.5 used simulated rollouts as prompts for a real robot on a subset of tasks, without another training run
insights.locator: Those evaluations can then guide

themes.theme: Simulation fidelity and scaling of environment creation

insights.claim: Simulation helps only if it preserves the real difficulty. If fingers pass through the microwave opening or unrealistic friction keeps the can on the gripper, more attempts only reinforce the wrong lesson.
insights.so_what: Physics fidelity, not just volume of synthetic data, determines whether sim-trained robots work.
insights.quote: If the fingers pass through the microwave opening, or unrealistic friction keeps the can attached to the gripper, generating more attempts only reinforces the wrong lesson.

insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: In SIMPLER, replaying a real robot's actions first produced a missed grasp in simulation, and calibrating the simulated controller was needed to reproduce the real grasp. Without that correction, a simulator error could be mistaken for a policy weakness.
insights.so_what: Uncalibrated simulators can produce misleading evaluation results, so real-robot checks remain necessary.
insights.quote: Without that correction, a team could mistake a simulator error for a weakness in the policy.

insights.claim: Useful simulation needs correct geometry, appearance, articulation and physical properties, and the details that matter depend on the task. If every new task needs weeks of manual construction and calibration, simulation inherits the scaling problem it was meant to solve.
insights.so_what: Tools that make reusable, calibrated sim environments quick to build are a key enabling layer for robotics.

themes.theme: Path to plug-and-play robots and projectsim's bet

insights.claim: Plug-and-play robots could arrive as foundation models bring larger skill repertoires, broad evaluation catches weaknesses before customers do, and AI systems work out what a job still needs. Progress should be measured by robots handling more jobs reliably with less specialist effort per job.
insights.so_what: Watch per-deployment engineering effort as the key metric of robotics commercialization.
insights.quote: The measure of progress is whether this preparation produces robots that handle more jobs reliably, with less specialist effort for each new one.
insights.locator: The measure of progress is whether
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio

insights.claim: projectsim is building simulations from assets and scenes where teams can run policies, generate experience and test new policies while reusing environments and varying tasks, without redoing simulation work each time.
insights.so_what: Simulation-as-a-service for robot policy training and evaluation is an emerging startup category.
insights.quote: A team should be able to reuse an environment, vary its tasks and test a new policy without starting the simulation work again.
insights.locator: This is what we are building
insights.speaker: Luca Cilio
